plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated tempo run for speed development.
Incorporates a strength session to improve trail-specific leg strength.
More balanced distribution of intensity types (tempo, aerobic, strength).
plan_b_advantages: Longer long runs, potentially building greater overall endurance.
More consistent easy running, which can be good for recovery and maintaining volume.
reasoning: Considering the goal of becoming a faster trail runner, Plan A is the better choice. It incorporates a dedicated tempo run, which is crucial for improving running economy and lactate threshold – key factors for speed. Plan B’s focus on extended easy runs, while beneficial for endurance, doesn’t prioritize the specific intensity work needed to boost pace. Plan A also includes a strength session, which is often overlooked but vital for trail running’s demands on leg strength and stability. While Plan B has longer long runs, Plan A’s structured approach to building speed is more directly aligned with the stated goal.
